report.summary: All four failures are 5-second timeouts on pages that render the book list: two on page.goto('/books'), one on the Add book submit, and one on the Register submit, which redirects to /books. The likely cause is the seeded slow_list bug (random 0-8 s delay in list_books), which makes these tests flaky rather than broken. First, confirm whether BUGS=slow_list was set for this run; if it was, either fix the app's listing latency or give navigation waits more headroom in the 5 s fixture.

causes.title: Book listing sometimes takes longer than the 5 s UI timeout
causes.explanation: list_books() sleeps for a random 0-8 s when the BUGS env var contains slow_list (app/main.py:160-161). render_books() calls list_books() on every /books render (app/main.py:270), and POST /register, POST /books and GET /books all end up rendering or redirecting to /books. The UI fixture sets the default Playwright timeout to 5000 ms (tests/ui/conftest.py:5-7). Whenever the random delay exceeds about 5 s, page.goto waits out its timeout, and clicks that trigger a navigation fail with 'waiting for scheduled navigations to finish'. The four failing tests are the ones whose first slow request hit a long delay. The UI tests that also load /books but drew a short delay pass, so the outcome changes from run to run. The app's own docstring labels this bug as flaky timing. The failures do not show a wrong result, only slowness. The run did not include BUGS, so I can't tell from the logs whether slow_list was active; the workflow file does not set it (.github/workflows/tests.yml:34-38), which points to a local or manually configured run.

causes.suggested_fix: 1) Check the BUGS environment variable used for this run; if slow_list was set, that explains the failures. 2) For CI, run the app with BUGS unset, or keep slow_list only in a dedicated, clearly labelled suite. 3) If the slow listing is meant to be tested, make the tests tolerate it: raise the navigation and click timeout for the UI suite (for example 15 s, or wait on the response with expect_response) instead of the blanket 5 s default. 4) Re-run the four listed tests several times to confirm they pass once the delay is removed.
